rationale.usefulness: Frozen pedagogical moments, matched tutor continuations and separate scaffold/rigor metrics directly address a practical failure in education software. Concrete regression, teacher-review and explainer workflows provide unusually useful next steps without claiming learning efficacy.
rationale.impact: Context-sensitive evaluation of when to help or hold back is a meaningful contribution to tutor development. The narrow population, synthetic students and model-assisted scoring bound its significance; the evidence does not establish better classroom outcomes or general AI progress.
rationale.novelty: Replay from teacher-selected decision points with fixed student traits provides meaningful differentiation from answer-correctness scoring. It extends existing simulation and behavior-evaluation methods rather than demonstrating an entirely new evaluation paradigm.
rationale.maturity: The released runtime, frozen records, prompts, manifests, failure handling and reference replays support practical evaluation. Preview scope, subjective/noisy labels and unrecoverable original human action classifications limit confidence in complete reproduction and external validity.
rationale.openness: Apache code, CC BY data, fixed contexts and provenance provide strong inspectability and reuse. Third-party model terms and credentials, residual de-identification risk, and the missing historical classification run prevent full openness and end-to-end reproducibility.

concerns: Original human action-distribution classifications are unavailable; current reference KL figures are not interchangeable with paper figures.
Scores measure behavior in selected synthetic replays, not real student learning or superiority to teachers.
Historical model results, rate dates and timing methods must not be treated as current universal rankings.
